title: Enciphered after all? Word-level text metrics are compatible with some types of encipherment
authors: Claire L. Bowern and Daniel E. Gaskell
venue: CEUR Workshop Proceedings 3313, International Conference on the Voynich Manuscript
summary: The open companion to K-012 applies 22 orthographic transformations to known texts and compares 42 released features. It includes reversible encipherment and deliberately lossy symbol conflation. The authors compare z-scored Euclidean distances and document how results depend on the underlying language and source text.
established: Section 2 and Table 1 distinguish reversible additions or substitutions from transformations that remove information. The panel includes a Crema-inspired reversal with nulls, alternatives replacing letters with bigraphs, and reductions of vowels or consonants.

Figures 1–3 and Section 4 report that some transformations approach particular manuscript features. For instance, vowel removal in an Uzbek example comes close on some position summaries and remains far away on entropy. The distances vary across Latin sources under the same transformation, and manuscript renderings are closer to each other than the comparison items shown in Figure 2.

The exploratory comparison uses 200-word excerpts at 100 iterations and a common feature family. The discussion records that no tested transformation matches the feature set throughout, and treats altered-text comparisons as evidence that several word-level statistics can coexist with known-source text.

data.detail: The public companion matrix contains 814 transformed rows across 37 underlying source labels and 22 named transformations. The figures and Methods refer to the paper's own comparison counts.

open.question: Does the fall in measured character entropy under reversible symbol expansion persist when normalized by the length of the original source, and does it remain unusual against matched padding and substitution controls?
open.check: Freeze reversible addB and the unambiguous suffix-addition rules from Table 1. Use known texts and report held-apart entropy in bits per output symbol and bits per source symbol at context lengths zero through eight. Keep word and line breaks unchanged. Match output alphabet and expansion rate in independent random-padding, deterministic-padding and substitution controls. Verify exact inversion and compare across disjoint source works before drawing a conclusion.
